Note on calibration: H1's high confidence is earned by the slope/rate evidence; the residual risk is that the same disk exhaustion is being triggered by a write pattern the deploy introduced, which the flat pre/post slope argues against but does not fully exclude.

The freshness of the round-2 evidence is confirmed — F18/F19/F25 endpoints are well before the 14:46 deploy and the log series runs to 15:59, so the pre-deploy baseline is real, and the only post-14:49Z gap (no WAL point after 14:49:47) cannot matter because the deploy-boundary interval is covered. events.summary: H1 (ledger-db storage exhaustion from a pre-existing, slot-retained WAL backlog) is the well-supported root cause. Every causal hop rests on verified evidence: the disk fill is monotonic from 12:00Z (83.66%) at a constant ~0.09 pct/min slope with NO step at the 14:46Z deploy (F18,F19,F20,F35); the inactive slot 'analytics_cdc' WAL backlog grew at ~2860 MB/min pre-deploy vs ~2417 MB/min post-deploy, no acceleration, with comparable ~3000 MB/min hours earlier (F23,F24,F25); no temp-file/WAL burst is logged before 15:01:01Z (F26,F27,F28,F37,F38); disk crossing to 100% at ~14:57–15:00Z coincides exactly with the error onset (F7,F13). Payment-service's own resources and bank-api errors are flat (F16, arguing against H3); zero config changes and only one deploy exist in the window (F1,F2,F42, against H4).
